exact_statement: For every integer s>=1 and every ternary row u on a finite uniform physical cube that is a signed sum of at most s disjoint affine-cell indicators with intrinsic quadratic phases, B(u)=sum_T uhat(T)^2 log2(1/uhat(T)^2) <= K_s E(u), where K_s=2s[log2(s)+(s-1)log2(64s^2)+3+log2(e)]. No bound on codimension, cell mass ratios, or spectral correlations is assumed. Thus any Boolean F(x,y) partitioned into at most M affine physical Y cells with a quadratic phase and an arbitrary CELL-DEPENDENT affine X-label map on each cell satisfies H(F)<=K_M I_Y(F) and H(S_Y|S_X)<=K_M I_Y(F), under every mixed physical restriction. The complete source class also has H(F)<=2^(M+1)I_Y and H(S_Y|S_X)<=2^M I_Y by the elementary bounded-phase/active-Y argument, so its better full rate is min(K_M,2^(M+1)). The optional integer X-degree bound d>=1 is retained when present. Fixed-M admission excludes fresh Boolean data tensor factors of F2 phase degree above M+1. Proper FOUR-cell rows have K_4=280+8log2(e)<292; complete four-phase-cell sources also have full rate32.
